Cautiously dovish overall. While the statement notes a strong labor market, it emphasizes sub-2% inflation and continued weakness in business fixed investment and exports. The macro literature highlights that investment shortfalls often drive cyclical slowdowns and account for declines in real GDP, making the weakness in capex particularly important for the outlook (investment function and spending in business cycles). With market-based inflation compensation low and survey expectations little changed, New Keynesian and VAR evidence (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido; Rudebusch; Sims; Zha) supports easing when inflation is below target and output gaps risk widening, given the central role of expectations in price-setting. The 25 bp cut, coupled with T-bill purchases and repo operations to maintain ample reserves, aligns with modern operating-procedure research and ample-reserves implementation aimed at stabilizing output and inflation when pressures are muted (McCallum & Nelson, monetary operating procedures; Svensson on stabilization policy). Overall tone: more cautious than the headline labor strength suggests.
